headline: Superhuman acquires AI authenticity service GPTZero to integrate into its AI assistant
summary: AI writing assistant Superhuman has acquired GPTZero, an AI identification business. This move aims to integrate detection tools into Superhuman Go, despite Superhuman also encouraging AI content generation.
details: Superhuman has acquired GPTZero, an AI identification business known for its hallucination and plagiarism detection services. GPTZero also provides a tool that displays the percentage of internet content generated by AI.

Superhuman plans to integrate GPTZero's capabilities into its Superhuman Go AI assistant. This integration aims to enhance Superhuman's existing efforts around AI and authenticity, with teachers and students remaining a priority audience.

The acquisition presents an interesting dynamic: Superhuman encourages AI content creation, while GPTZero specializes in detecting it. GPTZero noted that Superhuman would help place its tools where people are already reading and writing.

Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. Superhuman's Grammarly product, another AI writing assistant, also includes AI detection tools, though its aggressive push of AI features has previously drawn criticism.

headline_marked: [[MoEngage acquires Aampe]] for tens of millions, betting on AI agents for marketing
headline: MoEngage acquires Aampe for tens of millions, betting on AI agents for marketing
summary: Indian customer engagement firm MoEngage acquired San Francisco-based Aampe in an all-cash deal reportedly worth tens of millions of dollars, aiming to integrate AI agents for hyper-personalized marketing.
details: Indian customer engagement software firm MoEngage has acquired San Francisco-based startup Aampe in an all-cash deal. The transaction is reportedly worth tens of millions of dollars, as MoEngage bets on AI agents to become the future of marketing.

Founded in 2020, Aampe develops software that assigns a dedicated AI agent to each customer. This allows brands to personalize messaging based on individual behavior rather than traditional audience segments and campaign rules.

Aampe currently serves over 30 customers across the U.S., Europe, and Asia-Pacific, and grew its annual recurring revenue by 150% over the past year. MoEngage co-founder and CEO Raviteja Dodda stated the acquisition will help them win customers from rival marketing platforms like Salesforce and Adobe.

Dodda noted that a significant portion of MoEngage's growth comes from enterprise customers migrating from Salesforce Marketing Cloud and Adobe Experience Cloud. He hopes the Aampe acquisition will further accelerate this trend.

This acquisition aligns with a broader industry shift where software companies are embedding AI deeper into enterprise applications. The focus is moving beyond content generation tools towards agents making autonomous decisions, especially in marketing for targeting and messaging.

Aampe's technology is already utilized by major brands such as Swiggy, Grab, and Taxfix, some of which also use MoEngage's customer engagement platform. Approximately 20 Aampe employees will join MoEngage, bringing their total workforce to about 820 people.

The deal comes over six months after MoEngage raised $280 million through a mix of primary and secondary transactions. Aampe had previously raised around $28 million across three funding rounds from investors including Peak XV Partners.
